title: An invitation to build something different.
intro: A private conversation with the women who could help shape our future.

letter.heading: I don’t want to build this alone.
letter.body:
I’m bringing together a small founding circle of women with different strengths and a shared desire to build a better construction company.

This page is an invitation to explore what we could build together. Read it at your own pace, and if something sparks an idea, a question or a concern, send it to me at the bottom of the page. Honest feedback is exactly what I’m looking for.

whoWeAre.heading: Homes people can stay in. Women who build them.
whoWeAre.text: Level Headed Building Co. is a women-owned, women-led construction company beginning in Simcoe County, Ontario.

items.title: Build
items.text: Repairs, renovations, accessibility, panelized construction and housing-provider projects.

items.title: Train
items.text: Women-only skills events, trades training, mentorship, apprenticeships and leadership.

items.title: Lead
items.text: Connect tradeswomen, clients, community partners and future women leaders.

mission: To deliver dependable, well-managed construction and housing services while creating real opportunities for women to learn, work, lead and thrive in the building industry.
vision: A construction industry where women shape the work, lead the teams and build stronger homes and communities, with Level Headed recognized for both craftsmanship and opportunity.

whyItMatters.heading: Two problems. One better way.

items.title: Homeowners deserve better
items.text: Clear pricing. Reliable communication. Respectful service. Work done carefully in the homes people depend on.

items.title: Women deserve opportunity
items.text: Real access to trades careers, equipment and sites that work for them, skilled mentorship and pathways to decision-making.

whyItMatters.closing: Our answer is not a promise to do things differently. It is to design the company differently from day one.

fiveWays.heading: Five ways we make a difference.
fiveWays.text: Construction and maintenance fund real jobs. Training and community build a stronger workforce. Housing expands our long-term impact.

items.title: Build
items.text: Repairs, renovations, accessibility, panelized builds and additions.

items.title: Maintain
items.text: Unit turnovers, repairs and ongoing work for housing providers.

items.title: Train
items.text: Women-only homeowner workshops and trades-to-leadership pathways.

items.title: Connect
items.text: Women-owned trades, professionals, mentors and communities.

items.title: Create homes
items.text: ADUs, shared living and partner-led housing opportunities.

fiveWays.note: Every offering is launched against demand, qualified capacity, insurance, compliance and sustainable margins.

services.title: Housing turnovers
services.text: Vacancy repairs, patching, painting, flooring, fixtures, safety fixes and move-in readiness for co-ops, nonprofits and social housing.

services.title: Panelized construction
services.text: Panelized additions, accessory units and projects for our own builds and qualified external partners, with design and site coordination.

services.title: Accessibility & repairs
services.text: Ramps, rails, bathrooms, entrances, aging-in-place upgrades, maintenance and small-to-medium renovations.

training.title: Home maintenance nights
training.text: Women-only hands-on events: shutoffs, basic plumbing, drywall patches, caulking, seasonal checks and tool confidence.

training.title: DIY & repair workshops
training.text: Safe use of tools, hanging shelves, basic carpentry, simple repairs and knowing when to call a licensed professional.

training.title: Trades & leadership
training.text: Intro-to-trades, jobsite readiness, mentoring, future apprenticeships, trainer development and site leadership.

brand.title: Market the work
brand.text: Women-only homeowner events, housing-provider outreach, referral partnerships, site stories and clear service offers.

brand.title: Build an audience
brand.text: Our websites, local search, social media, workshops and authentic stories of women building.

brand.title: Create crew identity
brand.text: Branded workwear, hard hats, caps, hoodies, shirts and practical accessories that reinforce professionalism.

brandNote: Crew merchandise is a brand and culture tool, not assumed core revenue. Brand images and apparel shown are concepts, not photographs of an operating crew.

capital.title: Startup capital
capital.text: Founder contributions if agreed, retained earnings and modest startup reserves. No assumed personal guarantees.

capital.title: Grants & programs
capital.text: Explore women-in-trades, training, workforce development and small-business supports. Eligibility and timing require verification.

capital.title: Training partners
capital.text: Colleges, workforce agencies, trade associations and employers for facilities, instructors, placements or funded cohorts.

capital.title: Delivery partners
capital.text: Women-led trades, architects, engineers, suppliers, panelization fabricators and community organizations.

capital.title: Housing partners
capital.text: Social housing providers, co-ops, municipalities and nonprofit partners for turnovers, retrofits and housing projects.

capital.title: Commercial partners
capital.text: Referral relationships with seniors’ organizations, occupational therapists, property managers and housing providers.

capitalNote: Potential sources and partner categories only. No funding award, signed agreement or program eligibility is implied.

revenue.title: Early / core
revenue.text: Accessibility work; repairs; renovations; women-only home maintenance events; home-safety assessments.

revenue.title: Recurring / relationship
revenue.text: Social housing and co-op unit turnovers, maintenance contracts, vacancy refreshes and repeat property work.

revenue.title: Training / education
revenue.text: Paid women-only DIY and home-maintenance events, trades workshops, sponsored training and funded cohorts.

revenue.title: Professional / project
revenue.text: Project coordination, owner representation, construction planning and consulting linked to Level Headed projects.

revenue.title: Longer term / partner-led
revenue.text: Panelized builds for our own projects and partners, additions, ADUs, and partner-led housing delivery.

revenue.title: Optional brand revenue
revenue.text: Selective apparel and branded merchandise sales, only if demand and margins justify them.

revenueNote: These are opportunities to test, not guaranteed income. Each offering must earn its place through demand, capacity, risk and margin.

values.title: Straight
values.text: Tell the truth early, including mistakes.

values.title: Teach
values.text: Make learning part of every job.

values.title: Respect homes
values.text: Treat every client’s space with care.

promise: Every project has a scope, price, budget and accountable lead.
Site teams know who decides what, and when to escalate.
Estimating, purchasing, scheduling and job costing support the field.
Clients know what is happening, who is coming and what changed.
Women get appropriate gear, safe facilities and a visible route to leadership.

circle.heading: Different expertise. Shared ambition.

items.title: Construction
items.text: Journeypersons, carpenters, generalists, site leaders and trade-business owners.

items.title: Professional services
items.text: Design, engineering, estimating, permitting, accounting, legal and finance.

items.title: Training & community
items.text: Educators, mentors, workforce advocates and housing/community partners.

circle.closing: What matters most: sound judgment, shared values, complementary strengths and a willingness to help shape what comes next.

expectations.explore: Our first services and markets; standards and systems; training; partnerships; and the leadership structure we may need.
expectations.notPromised: No job, ownership stake, paid engagement or decision-making authority is offered simply by joining the circle. Future employment, trade work, advisory roles or ownership would be discussed individually and formalized in writing.

first90.title: Set up
first90.text: Convene founding women, confirm business structure, insurance and WSIB obligations, define service boundaries, vendor requirements and pricing.

first90.title: Test
first90.text: Open local inquiry channels, meet housing providers and trades partners, host or pre-sell a first women-only maintenance event, quote pilot work.

first90.title: Deliver
first90.text: Complete eligible pilot jobs, document margins and feedback, seek repeat turnover work, refine training offers and form a reliable delivery roster.

roadAhead.title: Start & validate
roadAhead.text: Form founding circle, validate insurance and compliance, price offers, approach housing partners and schedule first events.

roadAhead.title: First paid work
roadAhead.text: Deliver first qualified repair, accessibility and turnover projects, plus women-only homeowner workshops.

roadAhead.title: Repeat & expand
roadAhead.text: Build recurring housing contracts, panelized partnerships, site leadership and funded training capacity.

roadAhead.title: Grow with demand
roadAhead.text: Expand into larger builds, panelized delivery and housing projects when the work, people and financing support it.

roadNote: Start immediately with outreach and planning. Begin paid work only once operational requirements are in place.

whyYou.heading: You may be one of the women who helps define what this company becomes.
whyYou.text: Not because everything has already been decided. Because it hasn’t, and your experience could matter.

nextConversation.heading: Let’s talk about what we could build.

prompts: What you would need to know
